text.tspan: • Number badge = risk ID in the enterprise risk register (Table 11.1); left bar = risk category.
• Cell colour = risk score = Probability (1–5) × Impact (1–5); score bands below.
• Captions mark action zones: ACT NOW (upper-right) vs MONITOR (lower-left).
Scores of 16+ denote the enterprise-critical tier; 8 of 16 risks sit at High or above.
Critical-material supply shock — iridium shock, PGM stockpiling, catalyst IP (risks 1, 13, 14)
China dependency — stack export control, trade war, PLI undersubscription (risks 2, 7, 11)
Grid & water constraints — intermittency, pipeline infra, water stress (risks 3, 9, 12)
Demand & capital — LCOH, aggregation, offtake, utilisation, standards, skills, Type-IV (7 risks)
Taxonomy per Chapter 17.1 of the report; IDs trace to the companion workbook, Sheet 14.
Risk concentrates in the upper-right: eight of sixteen risks score High or above, and the four
binding risks — grid intermittency (5×4), LCOH parity gap (4×5), iridium supply shock (4×5) and
manufacturing under-utilisation (4×4) — can each, unmitigated, push the programme towards the
Mirage scenario. Exposure is simultaneous, not sequential: a PGM shock and a mandate delay can co-occur.
Read the upper-right as one correlated cluster, not four independent events.
1. Critical Materials Reserve under ANRF — USD 250m, 12-month PGM cover (hedges risks 1, 14).
2. Catalyst R&D Mission — ₹4,000 cr over 5 years, three national centres (retires 1, 13, 16).
3. 2026 green-H2 blending mandate — bankable offtake for SIGHT awardees (retires 5, 7, 8).
4. Captive RE + 4-hour battery + coastal desalination — lifts capacity factor to 70% (retires 3, 12).
Total mitigation cost USD 10–15bn over 5 years — c. 0.5–0.8× the NGHM outlay; the four priorities address 12 of 16 risks.
